<div class="learn-box">
**What you will learn**

Bind measurements at a common date, derive BMI, mean arterial pressure and a
ratio, and check the inputs needed for eGFR and duplicate handling.
</div>

**You need:** the Opal login from [Getting started](book-00-start.html) and the
recipe basics from [chapter 6](book-06-events.html). Run the sections in order:
each uses objects defined immediately above it. This chapter uses `omop.synthea`,
then `omop.questionnaire_formulas`.


## Find the inputs before calculating

Use the same Synthea resource as the lab chapter. A formula does not make inputs
comparable: check the measurement meaning, units and date before combining them.




``` r
library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.synthea", server = "site")$conns
```



Search weight and height separately and inspect their standard status. Select an exact name, not the first search hit.


``` r
weight_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Body weight", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
height_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Body height", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
rbind(weight_hits, height_hits)[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|----------:|:------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|    3025315|Body weight  |S                |LOINC         |
|    3036277|Body height  |S                |LOINC         |

``` r
weight_id <- weight_hits$concept_id[trimws(weight_hits$concept_name) == "Body weight"]
height_id <- height_hits$concept_id[trimws(height_hits$concept_name) == "Body height"]
body_sets <- list(weight = omop_concept_set(weight_id), height = omop_concept_set(height_id))
```

Body weight is **3025315** and Body height is **3036277**. Choosing the exact
name avoids mixing measurements with similar wording.


``` r
weight_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = weight_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
height_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = height_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
weight_units[c("value", "concept_name", "n")]
```



|value |concept_name |   n|
|:-----|:------------|---:|
|9529  |kilogram     | 510|

``` r
height_units[c("value", "concept_name", "n")]
```



|value |concept_name |   n|
|:-----|:------------|---:|
|8582  |centimeter   | 495|

The inventories identify **9529**, kilogram, for weight and **8582**, centimetre,
for height. The `value` column holds the unit concept ID; `n` is a record count
rounded down to a multiple of five.

## Bind weight and height on the same day

Index on first weight. The exact-day tolerance selects both inputs at that date.
An absent height stays missing; choosing a distant height silently would change
the formula's meaning. Synthea includes children, so do not apply adult BMI bands.


``` r
weight_event <- omop_event("measurement", body_sets$weight)
weight <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", body_sets$weight, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(9529L))
height <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", body_sets$height, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8582L))
```

## Declare a named BMI formula

The formula requires kilograms and metres. Declare the conversion from each
recorded unit into the physical unit the formula expects (called a *coordinate*
in the formula API). A factor of 0.01 converts centimetres
to metres; it is not a display-only rename.


``` r
weight_kg <- omop_number(weight, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:9529", "coordinate:kg", factor = 1)))
height_m <- omop_number(height, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8582", "coordinate:metres", factor = 0.01)))
bmi <- omop_formula_bmi(weight_kg, height_m)
body <- omop_study(weight_event, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(weight = weight, height = height, bmi = bmi))
recipe_execute(body, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_body"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_formula_body$bmi", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 28
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean
#> 11.53374 13.62216 15.88957 23.86380 27.93787 30.20849 30.36386 22.11315
```

The mean BMI is about 22.11 kg/m². BMI is kg divided by metres squared. The formula uses the presented coordinates,
requires positive finite inputs and records its equation and definition
in the codebook. Missing or invalid inputs become missing privately. Same-day
alignment remains a study decision; a formula does not create it automatically.

**Exercise 1.** Round BMI to one decimal for presentation while keeping the
unrounded formula available.

<details><summary>Solution 1</summary>


``` r
body_rounded <- omop_study(weight_event, outputs = "baseline",
  baseline = list(bmi = bmi, rounded = omop_number(bmi,
    omop_number_spec(rounding = omop_number_round("decimals", 1)))))
recipe_execute(body_rounded, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_rounded"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_formula_rounded$rounded", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 28
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean
#> 11.52000 13.60000 15.85000 23.85000 27.90000 30.19000 30.40000 22.10357
```

The rounded BMI mean is about 22.1 kg/m². The final presentation changes; the canonical BMI expression still uses its
unrounded inputs.

</details>

## Mean arterial pressure and a ratio

Find systolic and diastolic pressure, inspect their recorded units, then bind both
to the same systolic measurement date. The familiar approximate MAP formula is
(SBP + 2 × DBP) / 3; it is a derived estimate, not a separately measured pressure.


``` r
sbp_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Systolic blood pressure", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
dbp_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Diastolic blood pressure", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
rbind(sbp_hits, dbp_hits)[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name                          |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|----------:|:-------------------------------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|   40758413|Blood pressure systolic and diastolic |S                |LOINC         |
|    3004249|Systolic blood pressure               |S                |LOINC         |
|   40758413|Blood pressure systolic and diastolic |S                |LOINC         |
|    3012888|Diastolic blood pressure              |S                |LOINC         |

Both pressure searches also return panel **40758413**, Blood pressure systolic
and diastolic. Select the separate systolic (**3004249**) and diastolic
(**3012888**) measurements for the formula.


``` r
sbp_id <- sbp_hits$concept_id[trimws(sbp_hits$concept_name) == "Systolic blood pressure"]
dbp_id <- dbp_hits$concept_id[trimws(dbp_hits$concept_name) == "Diastolic blood pressure"]
pressure_units <- lapply(c(Systolic = sbp_id, Diastolic = dbp_id), function(id)
  ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = id,
    scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled[c("value", "concept_name", "n")])
do.call(rbind, pressure_units)
```



|          |value |concept_name              |   n|
|:---------|:-----|:-------------------------|---:|
|Systolic  |8876  |millimeter mercury column | 725|
|Diastolic |8876  |millimeter mercury column | 725|

Both pressures use **8876**, millimeter mercury (mmHg). Check both inputs:
a shared name for the result would not repair mismatched units.


``` r
sbp_event <- omop_event("measurement", omop_concept_set(sbp_id))
sbp <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", sbp_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8876L))
dbp <- omop_value_at_index("measurement", dbp_id, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8876L))
sbp_mmhg <- omop_number(sbp, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8876", "coordinate:mmHg", factor = 1)))
dbp_mmhg <- omop_number(dbp, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8876", "coordinate:mmHg", factor = 1)))
map <- omop_formula_map(sbp_mmhg, dbp_mmhg)
ratio <- omop_formula_ratio(sbp_mmhg, dbp_mmhg, unit = "1")
pressure <- omop_study(sbp_event, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(map = map, ratio = ratio))
recipe_execute(pressure, out = c(baseline = "D_formula_pressure"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_formula_pressure$map", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 28
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean
#> 85.70000 87.23333 90.08333 93.50000 95.75000 96.96667 99.40000 93.53571
```

The MAP summary describes the same-day formula, in mmHg; its mean is about
93.54. This is an approximation from two pressure readings.

**Exercise 2.** Summarise the dimensionless systolic/diastolic ratio. Is its unit mmHg?

<details><summary>Solution 2</summary>


``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_formula_pressure$ratio", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 28
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean
#> 1.220452 1.291128 1.316157 1.516234 1.612708 1.639932 1.726477 1.487598
```

The mean ratio is about 1.5. Its unit is not mmHg: the identical numerator and denominator units cancel. That does not make
ratios from different measurement definitions interchangeable.

</details>

## eGFR: validate the prerequisites before deriving

The race-free adult CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation needs serum creatinine,
age and sex. Its public formula is
142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^−1.2 × 0.9938^age,
with κ = 0.7 and α = −0.241 for female, κ = 0.9 and α = −0.302
for male, and a further factor 1.012 for female. Scr is in mg/dL.
See the [National Kidney Foundation equation](https://www.kidney.org/ckd-epi-creatinine-equation-2021).

Do not use urine measurements in place of serum measurements just to obtain a released result.
This check distinguishes vocabulary availability from observed use:

<!-- expected-refusal:start -->

``` r
creatinine_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Creatinine", domain = "Measurement",
  vocabulary = "LOINC", conns = conns)$pooled
creatinine_hits[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name                                  |standard_concept |
|----------:|:---------------------------------------------|:----------------|
|    3001802|Microalbumin/Creatinine [Mass Ratio] in Urine |S                |
|    3016723|Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma   |S                |
|    3051825|Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Blood             |S                |

``` r
serum_id <- creatinine_hits$concept_id[trimws(creatinine_hits$concept_name) ==
  "Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma"]
serum_set <- omop_concept_set(serum_id)
serum_locations <- ds.omop.concept.locate(serum_id, scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
serum_locations$per_site[[1]]
```



|table_name |concept_column | concept_id| n_records| n_persons|
|:----------|:--------------|----------:|---------:|---------:|

<!-- expected-refusal:end -->

The serum locator returns no releasable row. An empty locator result can mean
no records or too few people to release; it does not establish absence. The
public synthetic source has 12 serum/plasma creatinine records from one person,
which is below the release threshold. Blood creatinine is a different specimen,
and the first search hit is a urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio, a different
analyte. Neither is a substitute for suitable serum measurements.

The formula requires standardized serum creatinine in mg/dL, completed age at
measurement, and an explicit mapping to the equation's female/male branches.
It returns missing for children, nonpositive creatinine and unmapped sex. Save
the intended serum definition in a named project file before moving to the
separate questionnaire example. Saving lets later work reuse exactly the same
concept definitions.


``` r
formula_file <- "formula-concepts.rds"
formula_concepts <- list(body = body_sets, systolic = omop_concept_set(sbp_id),
  diastolic = omop_concept_set(dbp_id), serum_creatinine = serum_set)
saveRDS(formula_concepts, formula_file)
```

## Collapse repeated episodes deliberately

With `select = "all"`, every eligible weight reading starts a population episode.
A person can therefore have several episodes. Requesting person grain requires
an explicit collapse rule: first_episode, last_episode or any. This
collapses repeated population episodes, not duplicate source measurements.


``` r
episodes <- omop_population("weights", index = omop_index(weight_event, select = "all"))
collapsed <- omop_recipe(populations = list(episodes), variables = list(weight = weight),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "weights", format = "wide", grain = "person",
    collapse = "first_episode"))
recipe_execute(collapsed, out = c(people = "D_collapsed_weights"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_collapsed_weights$weight", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 28
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>       5%      10%      25%      50%      75%      90%      95%     Mean
#>  2.71000  3.73000 11.05000 70.90000 75.72500 80.94000 84.83500 50.44643
```

The first-episode weight mean is 50.45 kg. Selecting the closest reading chooses
one reading; averaging combines all eligible readings. A same-day window alone
does not decide how duplicates are combined. Document whether the problem is repeated episodes or duplicated source
records before choosing a collapse or reducer. The events chapter compares
record counts with distinct-day counts.

Compare the last eligible episode with the first one.



``` r
last_episode <- omop_recipe(populations = list(episodes), variables = list(weight = weight),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "weights", format = "wide", grain = "person",
    collapse = "last_episode"))
recipe_execute(last_episode, out = c(people = "D_last_weights"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_last_weights$weight", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 28
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>     5%    10%    25%    50%    75%    90%    95%   Mean
#> 12.630 16.850 64.325 75.000 82.300 89.630 94.365 66.600
```

The last-episode weight mean is 66.60 kg, compared with 50.45 kg at the first
episode. The Synthea population includes children growing across years, which
helps explain this large difference. Each person contributes their selected
episode; this is not an average over all measurements or episodes.

## Execute eGFR with declared synthetic inputs

`omop.questionnaire_formulas` holds synthetic standardized serum creatinine
measurements and explicitly named equation-sex categories. This is formula
practice, separate from the Synthea data. Its partial birth
dates remain incomplete so that missing age still produces missing eGFR.


``` r
ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.questionnaire_formulas", conns = conns)
```




``` r
formula_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Teaching standardized serum creatinine",
  domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
sex_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, domain = "Gender", conns = conns)$pooled
rbind(formula_hits, sex_hits)[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name                           |standard_concept |vocabulary_id |
|----------:|:--------------------------------------|:----------------|:-------------|
|     970001|Teaching standardized serum creatinine |S                |Questionnaire |
|       8532|FEMALE                                 |S                |Gender        |
|       8507|MALE                                   |S                |Gender        |

``` r
formula_id <- formula_hits$concept_id
formula_set <- omop_concept_set(formula_id)

ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = formula_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled[c("value", "concept_name", "n")]
```



|value |concept_name            |  n|
|:-----|:-----------------------|--:|
|8840  |milligram per deciliter | 45|

``` r
sex_ids <- setNames(sex_hits$concept_id, sex_hits$concept_name)
formula_concepts$questionnaire <- list(creatinine = formula_set, sex = sex_ids)
saveRDS(formula_concepts, formula_file)
```

Creatinine **970001** is a local teaching concept with no external mappings.
The equation branches use Female **8532** and Male **8507**.
The synthetic source explicitly defines standardized serum measurements in mg/dL.
The clinical equivalents would require assay and source validation.
With `missing = "keep"`, the first selected missing reading stays missing rather
than being skipped. With `scope = "episode"`, the age anchor is selected within
the current episode.


``` r
serum_event <- omop_event("measurement", formula_set, unit = omop_unit(8840L))
creatinine <- omop_variable(event = serum_event,
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", missing = "keep"))
creatinine <- omop_number(creatinine, omop_number_spec(unit =
  omop_number_unit("unit:8840", "coordinate:idms_creatinine_mg_dl", factor = 1)))
egfr <- omop_formula_egfr_ckdepi2021(creatinine,
  age = omop_age_at(omop_anchor(serum_event, which = "first", scope = "episode")),
  sex = omop_variable(table = "person", column = "gender_concept_id"),
  sex_map = list(female = paste0("concept:", sex_ids[["FEMALE"]]),
    male = paste0("concept:", sex_ids[["MALE"]])))
egfr_recipe <- omop_recipe(
  populations = omop_population("measurements", index = omop_index(serum_event)),
  variables = list(egfr = egfr),
  outputs = omop_output("people", rows = "measurements", format = "wide"))
egfr_result <- recipe_execute(egfr_recipe, out = "D_egfr", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.summary("D_egfr$egfr", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> $site$class
#> [1] "numeric"
#>
#> $site$length
#> [1] 48
#>
#> $site$`quantiles & mean`
#>        5%       10%       25%       50%       75%       90%       95%      Mean
#>  34.53919  34.53919  46.14291  99.23431 116.37404 118.71584 118.71584  86.11545
```

``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.numNA("D_egfr$egfr", datasources = conns)
```

```
#> $site
#> [1] 12
```

Mean eGFR is 86.12 mL/min/1.73 m². There are 36 valid estimates and 12 missing because of incomplete birth dates.
The output is an adult estimate in mL/min/1.73 m². Age is completed calendar years
at the selected creatinine measurement. Missing age or an unmapped equation-sex
category remains missing; the formula never guesses a branch or adds a race term.

**Exercise 3.** Inspect the formula and its unit retained with the table.

<details><summary>Solution: retain the equation and its eligibility rules</summary>


``` r
formula_record <- recipe_codebook(egfr_result)[[1]]$formulas[[1]]
formula_record[c("equation", "unit")]
```

```
#> $equation
#> [1] "142*min(Scr/k,1)^alpha*max(Scr/k,1)^(-1.200)*0.9938^age*sex_factor"
#>
#> $unit
#> [1] "coordinate:ml_min_1_73m2"
```

The equation and unit identify what was calculated. Keep the full formula record
with the saved codebook, including its adult eligibility rules.

</details>

## Collapse duplicate readings within a day

The questionnaire weights use concept **950002**, Body weight (questionnaire),
and unit **9529**, kilogram. With the formula data, 12 people have weights 60 and
72 kg on the same day, then 66 kg two days later. For them, daily mean then mean
is 66 kg; daily max then mean is 69 kg. The other measured groups have values
80 and 100 kg, and 12 people have no weight. Synthea weights have no same-day
duplicates, so they cannot demonstrate this difference.


``` r
weight_info <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(c(950002L, 9529L), conns = conns)$pooled
weight_info[c("concept_id", "concept_name")]
```



| concept_id|concept_name                |
|----------:|:---------------------------|
|     950002|Body weight (questionnaire) |
|       9529|kilogram                    |

The lookup confirms the questionnaire weight and kilogram IDs used below.


``` r
rows <- omop_number_rows(omop_event("measurement", 950002L, unit = omop_unit(9529L)))
daily <- omop_recipe(variables = list(
  daily_mean = omop_number_daily(rows, reducer = omop_reduce("mean"), within_day = "mean"),
  daily_max = omop_number_daily(rows, reducer = omop_reduce("mean"), within_day = "max")))
recipe_execute(daily, out = "D_daily", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_daily$daily_mean", datasources = conns)$Mean.by.Study
```



| EstimatedMean| Nmissing| Nvalid| Ntotal|
|-------------:|--------:|------:|------:|
|            82|       12|     36|     48|

``` r
dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_daily$daily_max", datasources = conns)$Mean.by.Study
```



| EstimatedMean| Nmissing| Nvalid| Ntotal|
|-------------:|--------:|------:|------:|
|            83|       12|     36|     48|

The overall means are **82 and 83 kg**, each based on 36 people, with 12 missing.
Only the first group's values change. Each observed day contributes once after
within-day reduction; absent days are not filled. Choose the rule for the study
question, because repeated readings can otherwise give a day extra weight.

## Recap

Align meanings, units and dates before arithmetic. Named formulas preserve
private inputs and declared units; missing prerequisites are a reason to stop a
formula study. Choose a collapse rule for repeated population episodes and a
separate within-day rule for duplicate readings.
